newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DRAB BARCELONA-REAL REOPENS SPANISH TITLE RACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DRAB BARCELONA-REAL REOPENS SPANISH TITLE RACE.

text.p: Several controversies have arisen in the wake of the big Barcelona-Real Madrid game but one thing not in doubt is that Saturday's match was one of the worst 'old firm' clashes on record.
Neutral fans can take comfort only in the fact that Barcelona's scrappy -- and at times violent -- 1-0 victory has at least added some excitement to the Spanish title race.
With five games left to play, Real hold a five-point lead over their arch-rivals.

However, Real's 2-0 home win over Barcelona earlier in the season means the gap is effectively six points, as standings of teams level on points are decided by the results of games played between them.
Both sides have tough run-ins.

Real must travel to Athletic Bilbao and Celta Vigo and face Valladolid, Extremadura and Atletico Madrid at home, while Barcelona play Celta, Hercules and Rayo Vallecano away and entertain Deportivo Coruna and Real Betis in the Camp Nou.
Barcelona's task looks tougher, as both Deportivo and Betis are still pressing for second place and with it a berth in next season's European Cup.
But few Real fans can forget that their side threw away substantial leads over Barcelona in successive years with defeats in the last game of the season at Tenerife.
Those games revived an old controversy in the Spanish game over bonuses paid to to third-parties.
The bonuses -- supposedly paid by teams to beat their rivals in championship or relegation battles -- are banned by the Spanish Federation but few people doubt their existence.
The coach of the only team still to play both Barcelona and Real Madrid, Celta Vigo's Fernando Santos, said that he would happily accept incentives to beat both sides.
But Santos's team may not need any extra incentive, as they are one of 11 sides still threatened with relegation.
The top 11 sides are still fighting out places in Europe.
Curiously champions Atletico Madrid look almost certain to take a UEFA Cup slot and may be uncommitted by the time of the Spanish capital's big derby game, the last match-but-one of the season.
But Atletico chairman Jesus Gil will be looking for revenge for January's defeat led by Real striker Raul Gonzalez.
"Let's see Raul if we pay back the 4-1 you handed us," Gil said.
Another key factor in deciding the championship may be suspensions and injuries to key players.
Yellow cards picked up in Saturday's clash mean that Barcelona's Albert Ferrer, Luis Figo and Hristo Stoichkov will all miss next weekend's game at Celta.
Also doubtful is midfielder Giovanni.
Giovanni was one of two players taken out of the game with uncompromising tackles by another Brazilian, Roberto Carlos.
The Real full-back will also miss his side's next game, at home to Valladolid, after clocking up his fifth booking of the season.
For many people, amongst them Barcelona coach Bobby Robson, Roberto Carlos was lucky to finish the game on the field.
The inexperienced match referee failed to clamp down on the over-physical play, re-opening a controversy over the selection of match officials.

Referee and linesmen are now picked randomly, a practice adopted only recently to quash rumours over impartiality. But many Spanish fans feel a more authoritative hand should have taken charge of the country's top game.
Greater discipline could also have been shown in the club president's box.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz nearly came to blows with a former Barcelona official and afterwards lashed out at his hosts.
"His behaviour has been disgraceful...He was ridiculous and I have never seen similar behaviour in a president's box," Sanz said.
Sanz added that the relationship between the two sides was 'broken' and that he would not return to the Camp Nou.
Sanz's opposite number Jose Luis Nunez had warmed up the atmosphere for the game in traditional fashion by suggesting that several Real strikers had offered themselves as signings to Barcelona.
Barcelona's current target man, Ronaldo, increased his goal-tally to 32, equalling a 54-year-old record for league goals scored for Barcelona.

But the Brazilian knocked in the winner after seeing his poorly-struck penalty saved by Real's German goalkeeper Bodo Illgner. Barcelona have already used four penalty-takers this season and the chances are that Robson could soon be looking for another.
